sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Replace the invented unknown IRI nltl:loadHeightParallelToFrame with the canonical controlled value nltl:loadPatchHeightParallelToFrame in the bottom-load-case orientation constraint; the deterministic vocabulary report is invalid until this is corrected. Preserve the prior valid applicability, owner/path, quantity-unit, frameProfileType, and comparison requirements, and ensure the demand-versus-strength query correlates each load case with its applicable structural-member owner rather than an arbitrary member linked to that case.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the applicability and constraint scope: target only applicable local frames—bottom members and transverse local frames in side structures—instead of requiring transverseFrameOrientation, plasticStrength, and a load case for every structuralMember. Preserve the declared ship→structuralMember→loadCase paths and require the bottom-only patch-load orientation condition on the applicable load case. Add the declared patchLoad, midspanPlasticCollapseLoad, plasticStrength, and combinedShearAndBendingDemand quantity/unit structures, using the canonical unit IRI http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloN rather than http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/KiloN. Constrain all quantity owners according to their canonical domains, encode combined demand <= plastic strength, and retain the plastic-strength relationship to the midspan plastic-collapse load with a tolerance appropriate to the expected derived value. Do not introduce an unrelated universal frameProfileType obligation; if the dependency contract requires that relationship, model it only with an evidence-backed applicability rather than as a blanket ship requirement.

Semantic validator feedback: Add the COMPLETE dependency-contract relationship nltl:frameProfileType on the supplied ship owner, using the canonical term and its declared range/controlled value structure; do not impose it on structural members or invent a blanket unrelated obligation. Preserve the existing applicable-member branching, canonical ship→structuralMember→loadCase paths, quantity/unit constraints, combined-demand ≤ plastic-strength comparison, midspan-load relationship with derived-value tolerance, and bottom-only patch-load orientation.

Repair the direct-static applicability and owner/path checks while preserving the prior valid frameProfileType, canonical ship→structuralMember→loadCase paths, quantity/unit structures, demand <= plasticStrength comparison, midspan-collapse relationship with expected-value tolerance, and bottom-only patch orientation. The SPARQL has a bound-variable error: replace ?missingMemberLoad with ?missingCase when checking midspanPlasticCollapseLoad. Explicitly fail an applicable member that has no hasStructuralMemberLoadCase, rather than only checking cases that exist; require all declared operands on that applicable member/case. Do not let a side-structure member with missing transverseFrameOrientation silently become inapplicable; encode the conditional side-frame applicability and xsd:boolean evidence so absent selection evidence cannot pass. Scope combined-demand and load-case constraints to applicable members instead of unconditionally constraining every target object of hasStructuralMemberLoadCase. Ensure midspanPlasticCollapseLoad and plasticStrength are checked on their declared structuralMember owner, combinedShearAndBendingDemand and loadPatchOrientation on the declared loadCase owner, and patchLoad on the declared ship owner.
